title: Minimum Swaps for Couples Holding Hands
hints: seats come in fixed pairs: (0,1), (2,3), (4,5), and so on. for each pair, you know exactly which value the second seat should hold once you know the first seat's value. how would you place that value in a single pass?
keep a map from value to its current seat, so you can find any specific person in O(1) instead of scanning

walk through seat pairs left to right. for seat 2k, compute the partner value it needs (partner of row[2k]). if row[2k+1] isn't already that partner, swap the partner into seat 2k+1, updating the position map, and count one swap
this greedy placement, one seat-pair at a time, guarantees the minimum swap count because every swap permanently fixes one couple without breaking any already-fixed couple
commonMistakes: not updating the value-to-position map after each swap, causing later lookups to point at stale seats
computing the wrong partner formula (partner of v is v+1 if v is even, v-1 if v is odd, i.e. v XOR 1)
trying to solve with a general graph cycle-counting approach when a simpler greedy linear scan suffices and is easier to get right

content.problemStatement:
There are n couples sitting in a row of 2n seats. Couple i is
represented by the two values 2i and 2i+1 (so couple 0 is values 0 and
1, couple 1 is values 2 and 3, and so on). The row is given as an
array `row` where `row[k]` is the value of the person sitting in seat k.
In one swap you may pick any two people and swap their seats.

**Return the minimum number of swaps needed so that every couple ends up sitting in adjacent seats.**
constraints: row contains every integer from 0 to row.length - 1 exactly once
couple i consists of the values 2i and 2i + 1
notes: already fully paired, requiring zero swaps
a single couple (n = 1, trivially 0 swaps needed)
a chain of several couples that are all mutually displaced, requiring multiple swaps

couple (2,3) already sits together at positions 0-1, and couple (0,1) already sits together at positions 2-3
swap positions 1 and 2 so row becomes [0, 1, 3, 2], now both couples are adjacent

optimal.pattern: cyclic sort style greedy placement over seat-pairs: walk seat pairs left to right, and whenever a seat's partner isn't next to it, swap the correct partner into place directly (using a value-to-position map for O(1) lookup), same spirit as placing each value at its target slot

bruteForce.approach: model each couple as a graph node and each seat-pair mismatch as an edge, then count edges needed to break all cycles; or simulate swaps greedily by scanning seat pairs and searching the rest of the array for the missing partner
